findings: The review was performed against an archive snapshot of immutable implementation 3fb74a8bf518a528e89686d1390c223983fc98fb with only the six fresh review-5 arrow fixture files copied in. The shared worktree's unrelated state.rs and route-identity files were not used for Rust validation.

Java provenance still supports the ordinary shared-arrow model. SkinParam.setParam runs cleanForKey for each declaration before both params storage and FromSkinparamToStyle conversion. cleanForKeySlow lowercases, removes underscores and dots, rewrites activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefixes to arrow, and FromSkinparamToStyle maps arrowColor to SName.arrow LineColor.

Rust commit 3fb74a8b implements the claimed ordinary alias storage model in parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams: ordinary records compare through canonical_skinparam_key, and when that identity is arrowcolor the surviving SkinParam.key is stored as arrowcolor. This fixes the prior review-4 boundary where final UseCase.Arrow_Color was retained as usecasearrowcolor and invisible to state rendering.

The renderer consumers inspected are consistent with that ordinary storage model for current primary paths. State and class reverse-scan state/classArrowColor or ArrowColor, and lowercase arrowcolor matches ArrowColor case-insensitively. Component and activity consume lowercase arrowcolor. Usecase consumes arrowColor through a case-insensitive helper. Sequence consumes lowercase arrowcolor, sequencearrowcolor, and classarrowcolor. The review-5 component and sequence heldouts both show inherited ordinary cross-family aliases reaching Rust as #2E7D32.

Synthetic theme body records remain isolated in Rust source. parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams keys theme-body replacement as theme:<segment>:<raw lowercased key> and does not canonicalize the family-arrow prefix. The reddress-lightred source expands family blocks such as class/usecase/activity/sequence/state arrow_style(), while the component block omits arrow_style(). Rust therefore does not merge those non-component theme keys into ordinary arrowcolor.

That isolation is source-faithful to the corrected account but not enough to pass the strict Java oracle for the fresh component theme negative. Pinned Java renders inherited component arrows #000000 for review5_component_theme_scope_negative, while Rust remains #181818. This rejects the heldout under the no-oracle gate even if it supports the claim that Rust did not leak synthetic theme family keys into component arrow state.

The strongest mechanism-shaped rejection is the sequence local override. In review5_sequence_repeated_theme_cross_family_alias, Java applies the final ordinary UseCase alias to inherited arrows (#2E7D32) and the local message override to the middle arrow (#C2185B dashed). Rust matches the inherited #2E7D32 arrows but renders the middle message #FFFFFF solid, so local link override semantics do not survive the requested cross-family/repeated-theme perturbation.

The component cross-family heldout also fails strict no-oracle comparison. Its emitted inherited Rust arrows use the final ordinary Activity.Arrow_Color #2E7D32, but the component no-oracle renderer lays out and orders entities/links differently from Java, so the strict comparator rejects the fixture before the mechanism can be accepted.

No production code, existing fixtures, baselines, guards, comparator slack, park/error lists, or state-parallel-transition-route-identity files were modified by this review. The only intended shared-tree additions are this review record and the six fresh review5 state-arrow-style-isolation perturbation files.

Verdict is rejected. A later implementation can still be on the right track for ordinary arrowcolor storage, but the mechanism cannot be accepted while the required valid-syntax perturbations fail strict no-oracle comparison, especially the sequence local colour/style override and the component theme-scope control.
